stories.head: ThoughtSpot's AgentSpot prices AI agents by business outcome, not by seat
stories.plain: ThoughtSpot's AgentSpot shifts the pricing model for enterprise AI from per-seat licenses to outcome-based billing — you pay when the agent delivers a result. That's a fundamental change to how marketing AI is bought and budgeted. It also signals a market move from single-user chatbots toward coordinated multi-agent AI workforces sharing data across a company.

stories.head: Limelit launches agentic GEO platform with 211 tools and MCP server for autonomous content workflows
stories.plain: Limelit connects Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor to an MCP server that tracks brand visibility across six AI search engines and runs governed agents that automatically fill content gaps. This matters because it turns GEO from a manual audit task into an always-on agentic workflow, changing how marketing teams staff and govern AI-search strategy.

stories.head: EngageLab's Agent Email lets AI agents receive, interpret, and reply to inbound customer email at scale
stories.plain: Aurora Mobile's Agent Email gives AI agents a real inbox — they read replies, pull answers from a private knowledge base, and write intent signals back to CRM, all while staying threaded in Gmail and Outlook. This moves agentic AI from outbound sending to two-way conversation handling, which reshapes how CEPs are built and governed.

stories.head: Personalization that knows what customers want matters more than knowing who they are
stories.plain: This piece argues that intent-based personalization — showing relevant offers based on current behavior — outperforms identity-based targeting that demands personal data upfront. It matters for practitioners because it reframes the CDP-vs-anonymous-signal debate: you can deliver meaningful 1:1 experiences without requiring consumers to identify themselves first.

stories.src: Agile Brand · via Agile Brand Guide
stories.head: Kochava caps AI token spend; Disco pays $3.50 per Shopify checkout offer in daily martech roundup
stories.plain: Three short signals worth tracking: Kochava introduces AI token-spend caps — a governance control on runaway LLM costs; ThoughtSpot prices AgentSpot by outcome (covered separately); and Disco pays merchants a fixed fee per AI-surfaced Shopify offer, signalling performance-linked AI commerce models. Together they show governance and new pricing structures reshaping how AI tools are procured.

stories.head: Salesforce acquires Braze for $5.7 billion — combining CRM giant with leading CEP
stories.plain: Salesforce is buying Braze, a major customer engagement platform, for $5.7 billion. This reshapes how enterprise marketing stacks are bought: brands that built around Braze must now consider a tighter Salesforce lock-in, while competitors race to fill the independent CEP space. It is one of the biggest martech acquisitions in years.

stories.head: Limelit launches agent-first GEO platform with MCP server and 211 automated tools
stories.plain: Limelit lets Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI assistants plug directly into its platform via an MCP server to track brand visibility across six AI search engines and automatically close content gaps. It is the first purpose-built agentic platform for generative engine optimization, signalling that GEO is moving from manual monitoring to autonomous execution.

stories.head: EngageLab's Agent Email lets AI agents receive, read, and reply to customer emails at scale
stories.plain: Aurora Mobile's Agent Email is infrastructure that gives AI agents a real email inbox: they receive inbound replies, understand intent, answer from a private knowledge base, and write signals back to CRM — threaded inside Gmail and Outlook. This extends agentic AI into two-way customer conversation, not just outbound sending.

stories.head: ChatGPT drives less than 1% of Google's traffic volume but converts at a higher rate
stories.plain: New data shows Google organic still delivers 27 times more conversions than all LLMs combined, yet ChatGPT visitors convert at a higher rate per click. For marketers deciding how much to invest in GEO versus traditional SEO, this gives the clearest benchmark yet — AI search matters at the margin, not at scale, today.

stories.head: Peec AI launches Peec Agent to let marketing teams act directly on AI search brand gaps
stories.plain: Peec Agent goes beyond reporting: it surfaces evidence-backed recommendations across technical, content, and third-party channels and then helps teams execute fixes against how AI search engines represent their brand. Used by 3,500 companies, this is a sign that GEO tooling is maturing from dashboards into agentic workflows.

themes.head: AI Agents Take the Wheel Across the Full Marketing Stack
body: Autonomous AI agents are no longer a future concept — they are shipping inside email, content, CRM, and fan-engagement platforms right now. Tools like EngageLab's Agent Email, Peec Agent, and AgentSpot show vendors racing to move AI from generating outputs to owning workflows end-to-end, including receiving and replying to customer messages without human review.

The critical infrastructure question that follows is data integrity: agents are only as trustworthy as the source of truth they query. Marketers who haven't audited and unified their data layer will find that agentic speed amplifies errors rather than efficiency, making data governance the new prerequisite for any AI rollout.
ev: MarTech · Build a source of truth for AI agents

themes.head: MCP Becomes the Universal Connector for AI & Martech
body: The Model Context Protocol is quietly becoming the API layer that lets external AI agents reach inside marketing tools — Framer, GeeLark, and Limelit all shipped MCP servers this month. This is a structural shift: instead of custom integrations, any capable AI agent can now manipulate websites, run cloud-phone workflows, or automate GEO tasks through a single open protocol.

For marketing technology buyers, MCP support is becoming a new evaluation criterion alongside REST APIs and webhooks. Platforms that expose MCP servers gain instant compatibility with the expanding universe of AI agents, while those that don't risk being bypassed entirely as orchestration moves to the agent layer.

themes.head: AI Search Visibility Replaces SEO as the Discoverability Battleground
body: As AI search engines convert user prompts into curated recommendations, the old playbook of ranking for keywords is giving way to a new game: being the brand AI models cite and surface. Creator content, product descriptions, and structured data are now training signals for AI recommendations, not just ranking factors — a reality reflected in tools like Peec Agent and Limelit being built specifically to monitor and improve AI-driven brand visibility.

The CommerceIQ CEO's framing of discoverability as the new digital shelf captures the stakes: if your product content doesn't inform AI search results, you lose the sale before a human even sees your listing. Marketers need to treat generative engine optimisation (GEO) with the same budget seriousness they once gave paid search.

themes.head: Personalization Shifts to Intent Over Identity
body: A quiet but consequential pivot is underway: leading practitioners are abandoning identity-first personalisation — built on cookies, logins, and profiles — in favour of behavioural signal and in-session intent models that infer what someone wants right now. This approach sidesteps privacy constraints and performs better in a world where third-party data is unreliable.

The same shift appears in how analysts talk about customer journeys: MarTech's framing of moving from journeys to decisions reflects a real-time, context-first model where the unit of analysis is a single choice moment rather than a mapped funnel. Martech stacks that can't act on live intent signals will struggle to compete with those that can.

themes.head: Composable & Insight-Ready Stacks Become a Leadership Demand
body: CEOs are asking questions that rigid, monolithic martech dashboards cannot answer — and that gap is now a boardroom problem, not just a technical one. The push toward composable architectures is driven as much by the demand for ad-hoc strategic insight as by integration flexibility, forcing CMOs to rebuild their stacks around modular, API-first components that can be queried in new ways.

At the same time, the industry is grappling with an AI governance & skills deficit that hiring and tooling alone won't close. Lessons from email marketing's regulatory history are being applied to AI deployment, and marketers are being told that competency frameworks — not just tool subscriptions — are what separate teams that scale AI responsibly from those that create liability.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack, the month's news tells the same story: the unit of marketing is shifting from campaign to autonomous decision, and organisations that haven't unified their data, embraced open protocols like MCP, and rethought visibility for AI-driven search will find themselves optimising for a world that no longer exists.
